# Java and Angular over the Spec's Python Stack

**Decision.** Build the ModellingClub platform on **Java 21 + Spring Boot + Angular**, even though
lab 1's own requirements specification proposes **Linux / Python / PostgreSQL / Nginx**.

**Date.** From lab 2 onward — the first Spring Boot service lands 2026-04-14, the same day as the
requirements document it diverges from.

## The choice, and the principle behind it

> "Interestingly, the document proposes a Linux / Python / PostgreSQL / Nginx deployment stack — but
> the labs deliberately satisfy the **same requirements** using a Java + Angular stack. The
> requirements are the contract; the technology is a choice."
> — Information-Systems-Modelling/README.md, 2026-07-25

That last clause is the decision. The SRS is treated as a **statement of obligations**, not a
statement of implementation — actors, functional and non-functional requirements, hard limits on
upload size and files per build, GDPR and EU drone compliance. None of those obligations mention a
language, so none of them are violated by changing one.

The word "deliberately" matters: this is the repo declaring a known, chosen divergence rather than
quietly building something else and hoping no one diffs it.

## What was rejected and what replaced it

| lab 1 SRS proposes | labs 2–7 deliver |
|---|---|
| Python | Java 21 |
| *(implied Python web framework)* | [[spring-boot]] 3.5.6 |
| PostgreSQL | SQLite (lab 2) → [[h2-database]] file mode (labs 3–4) |
| Nginx | none — `spring-boot-maven-plugin`, no deployment |
| *(no frontend named)* | [[angular]] 21.2 standalone + SSR |

PostgreSQL is the interesting row, because it was never fully abandoned: `application-prod.properties`
carries a commented-out PostgreSQL + HikariCP + Flyway block, and lab 7 models the H2 → PostgreSQL
changeover as a full BPMN process — see [[bpmn-process-modelling]]. The spec's database is *modelled
and planned for*, just never run.

## What the divergence cost, and what it bought

**Bought:** the OpenAPI toolchain of [[contract-first-api-design]] — `openapi-generator-maven-plugin`
emitting Spring interfaces from the contract — and, with it, the reason lab 4 needed
[[aspect-oriented-programming]] to add cross-cutting behaviour without hand-editing generated code.
A Python stack would have produced a different, probably thinner, set of labs.

**Cost:** the requirements-to-implementation link became purely narrative. **No lab file cites a
requirement id.** There is no traceability matrix, and the SRS's numbering (if it has any) is not
referenced anywhere in labs 2–7. The claim "the same requirements are satisfied" is therefore
asserted, not demonstrated — and lab 3 is a concrete case where it is *not* true: its contract
promises JWT authentication with bcrypt that the code does not implement. See
[[stateless-jwt-authentication]].
